assumptions.summary: Turnover is contagious and structurally similar employees affect one another.
Limited personnel data are replaced by explicit office-allocation principles.
Annual salary represents employee ability and signed weights combine assignment criteria.
Personnel edges follow three co-office, same-level, or sibling-leader rules with an unspecified sigma weight.
Salary and promotion prospect are constant within hierarchy groups.
Service time follows a truncated Gaussian and virtual-vacancy similarity represents work experience.
Monthly turnover and recruitment counts are Poisson, and a recruit restores deleted links.
All qualified employees are promoted immediately in Task 5.
A hometown relation is proposed as a second layer on the same employees.
Annual evaluation and position requirements share a Euclidean vector space.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The assignment-to-network handoff converts missing relations into an auditable modeling sequence.
The Production Manager/VP surprise shows why a graph metric can add information beyond formal hierarchy.
The month-6/month-8 comparison connects a contagion mechanism to a visible subgroup effect.

language_observations.summary: The human style comes from visible information gaps, reasons tied to method choice, explicit output handoffs, topology surprises, concrete curve mechanisms, same-scale scenario decisions, random-fluctuation admissions, and final data boundaries.

the Summary answers each task with a named mechanism and an inspectable output: Open with a dynamic HCN, then move task by task from assignment and network construction through contagion, productivity, budget, occupancy, promotion, and extensions.

team chemistry becomes a state-based Human Capital Network: Begin with the practical need to keep trained people in suitable positions, introduce turnover as the disturbance, and enumerate the network, centrality, salary, promotion, and stochastic state needed to study it.

a limited mathematical-turnover literature motivates a network program: Separate team-performance, multilayer-network, and contagion precedents, identify the missing quantitative turnover model, and hand that gap to the HCN program.

limited personnel data trigger explicit allocation rules before modeling: State the information gap, disclose the simplifying assignment rules, quantify them with AHP-style criteria, and use the resulting assignment to recover co-office relations.

qualitative assignment principles are converted into a signed objective: List centrality, hierarchy, equality, and uniformity, define one score for each, explain the scale imbalance, and combine them with positive and negative coefficients.

problem class and representation fit justify the Genetic Algorithm: Call the assignment combinatorial, compare search heuristics, observe that an assignment is already a gene code, and use swaps to implement crossover before reading the organizational result.

one model output becomes the next model's missing input: Treat the optimized office assignment as newly deduced information, combine co-office and supervisory relations, and turn employees and offices into the two HCN graphs.

a visual hierarchy surprise separates formal rank from topological importance: Construct the directed organizational graph, encode LeaderRank as node size, notice that Production Manager outranks VP despite hierarchy, and carry topology rather than title into employee importance.

literature categories are narrowed into four turnover factors: Start from external and internal correlates, specify salary, position level, and promotion prospect, add contagion from other employees, and use AHP to combine their contributions.

structural equivalence and attenuation turn one departure into a time-varying pressure: Interpret common neighbors as resource transmitters, revise the weighted RA index, sum similarity from former employees, and attenuate their influence with a logistic curve.

an interpretable network meaning justifies the centrality measure: Link centrality to workplace information and support, choose closeness because it represents time to reach others, combine it with department LeaderRank, and invert the product into turnover pressure.

static scores become turnover, promotion, and recruitment events: Use turnover intention as sampling weight, service time and virtual-vacancy similarity as promotion disciplines, and median recruiting time as a Poisson rate before refreshing network links.

figures separate a direct staffing loss from indirect network effects: Read the month-6/month-8 propagation, identify high mid-level intention, follow falling staff and repeated churn shocks, and quantify the final average-productivity reduction.

different curve shapes explain the two budget components: Attribute recruiting-cost spikes to Poisson arrivals, attribute smooth training decline to staff count and levels, and then report recruiting, training, and total requirements on one scale.

same-axis churn scenarios turn trajectories into an occupancy decision: Plot 18%, 25%, and 35% churn together, explain faster staffing loss and feedback through turnover intention, and conclude whether the 80% staffing target is sustained.

unavoidable random fluctuation is disclosed before a bounded robustness statement: Vary service-time distribution parameters, compare promoted count, productivity, senior-manager productivity, and manager count, admit that randomness cannot be eliminated, and limit the conclusion to small changes.

an omitted relationship becomes a new layer rather than an inflated single edge: Acknowledge that the HCN contains only internal links, add a hometown layer on the same nodes, compare information unique to each layer, and propose Jaccard overlap for group analysis.

an HR request is reduced to a transparent nearest-position rule: Represent annual evaluation and job requirements as vectors, define Euclidean distance, interpret larger distance as poorer fit, and choose the minimum-distance position.

broad strengths are followed by concrete data and grouping limits: Claim comprehensiveness, robustness, and interpretability, then admit grouped personnel categories and common-sense parameters caused by missing data.

results_trace.summary: The GA produces an assignment that visually respects hierarchy, equality, and uniformity after 500 random initial solutions.
Production Manager has a larger LeaderRank node than VP despite formal hierarchy.
Turnover pressure propagates through similar nodes and is visually higher for mid-level positions.
Average productivity is reported 9.8% lower after two years while repeated churn shocks remain visible.
Recruiting requires 19.14 sigma and training 10.87 sigma, totaling 30.01 sigma over two years.
Higher churn produces faster staff loss; plotted month-24 levels are roughly 258, 218, and 162 for 18%, 25%, and 35%.
Immediate promotion preserves upper-level productivity but creates a low-level employee shortage.
The sigma and mu sensitivity tables are visually identical, so only a bounded, unresolved robustness claim is retained.
Multiplex overlap and Euclidean HR matching are proposed but not empirically executed.
The paper ends by admitting grouped personnel categories and common-sense parameters due to few data.

source.title: Analyzing Employee Turnover Using Dynamic Network

source_quality.summary: All 20 pages were read twice and visually reviewed. The paper moves from limited personnel data through assignment optimization, two network views, four-factor turnover intention, stochastic personnel events, productivity/budget/scenario results, multiplex and HR extensions, and explicit final data limits.

decisions: how employees are assigned, who is more likely to leave, how vacancies are filled, whether 80% staffing is sustained, and what additional relations or HR matching are needed
inputs: 370-person roster, office hierarchy, salary ability proxy, graph rules, AHP judgments, service thresholds, recruiting/training information, and churn scenarios
outputs: employee assignment, two HCN graphs, turnover ranking, monthly staff/productivity traces, two-year budget, occupancy comparison, promotion effect, and extension proposals

title: Analyzing Employee Turnover Using Dynamic Network
unresolved_questions: The Summary reports a complete HCN, budget, occupancy, and promotion story, but every headline result remains internal to an uncalibrated simulation.
Related Work visibly retains [NOT good...], an ellipsis, (??), and an unfinished final clause; these draft remnants are excluded from positive language evidence.
The paper reconstructs personnel relations from limited information and reuses closeness notation before specifying disconnected-node handling or observed assignments.
Salary is treated as ability, equality/uniformity scales are not defined, and signed objective weights are chosen after unspecified random experiments.
The Genetic Algorithm uses 500 random initial solutions but reports no seed, population operators, stopping criterion, optimum gap, or comparison with the mentioned Tabu Search.
The personnel edge rule leaves sigma undefined, mixes three relationship conditions, and supplies no empirical tie-strength validation.
The organizational graph adds an artificial sink for LeaderRank, but the LeaderRank recurrence, initialization, damping, sink handling, and convergence trace are absent.
The revised RA similarity and logistic decay are not calibrated; beta, departure-time indexing, direct-neighbor behavior, and similarity normalization are under-specified.
Closeness and LeaderRank are combined by an inverse product without a disconnected-component policy, scale check, or empirical link to turnover.
The AHP judgment matrix is not strictly reciprocal, the text calls the score Equation (4) although it is labeled (2), and the reported CI/CR cannot substitute for a released calculation.

Employee efficiency is said to be inversely proportional to turnover intention but is not defined; cost units and provenance are missing, and the training-cost explanation mistakenly says recruiting costs.
The Poisson paragraph omits the promised monthly parameter statement, does not report seeds or fit evidence, and leaves the new-worker link reconstruction ambiguous.
The truncated-Gaussian promotion model clips service time and omits Administrative Clerks and Senior Managers without validating the distribution, interval widths, or eligibility consequences.
Figures 5-7 show one simulation path with no replications, uncertainty bands, raw series, or observed productivity outcome; the 9.8% reduction is therefore scenario-specific.
The budget uses sigma as a cost scale while later sensitivity uses sigma as a distribution parameter; source costs, units, seeds, and forecast error are not supplied.
The text says 25% and 35% churn cannot sustain 80% staffing, but the plotted 18% path also ends well below 80% of 370, so the decision boundary is internally unclear.
Tables 3 and 4 repeat exactly the same four output rows and values under sigma and mu, and the mu headers remain l, 2l, 3l; the second sensitivity claim is not independently supported.
The multiplex and HR extensions are illustrative: hometown ties, evaluation dimensions, vector scaling, Euclidean suitability, clustering interpretation, and fairness are not validated.
The final strengths infer rationality and correctness from common sense, while the explicit weaknesses admit grouped personnel categories and common-sense parameters caused by few data.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Make three turnover mechanisms inspectable.
visualization_observations.exact_reading: Revised RA similarity feeds a logistic departure influence, while employee closeness and department LeaderRank feed an inverse centrality factor.
visualization_observations.next_action: Define beta, components, normalization, direct neighbors, and scale sensitivity.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Expose the factor synthesis.
visualization_observations.exact_reading: Figure 4 connects contagion, employee centrality, salary, and promotion prospect to employee alternatives, followed by a visibly nonreciprocal judgment matrix and score labeled (2).
visualization_observations.next_action: Repair the matrix, recompute CI/CR and weights, and correct the equation reference.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Bind promotion eligibility to position level.
visualization_observations.exact_reading: Table 2 gives SM/JM/ES/IS/EE/IE thresholds 8/5/3/2/1/0 and excludes Administrative Clerks and non-promotable Senior Managers.
visualization_observations.next_action: Validate thresholds, units, truncation, and exclusion consequences.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Turn a network mechanism into a temporal visual comparison.
visualization_observations.exact_reading: Figure 5 shows a departure-pressure cluster moving through structurally similar nodes and labels relatively high mid-level turnover intention.
visualization_observations.next_action: Release node identities, raw intention values, seeds, and replications.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Separate direct staff loss from indirect intention effects.
visualization_observations.exact_reading: Figures 6 and 7 show declining level contributions, higher middle-manager intention, repeated shocks, and a reported 9.8% average-productivity reduction by month 24.
visualization_observations.next_action: Provide raw series, uncertainty bands, and observed productivity.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Explain curve shape before summing budget.
visualization_observations.exact_reading: Figure 8 shows volatile recruiting cost and smooth declining training cost, which the prose attributes to Poisson arrivals versus staff composition.
visualization_observations.next_action: Release cost units, source values, event counts, and seeds.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Turn same-scale scenarios into an occupancy check.
visualization_observations.exact_reading: Figure 9 compares 18%, 25%, and 35% on one axis; approximate month-24 levels are about 258, 218, and 162, all below 80% of 370.
visualization_observations.next_action: Reconcile the prose boundary and state tolerance and uncertainty.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Show the downstream staffing cost of immediate promotion.
visualization_observations.exact_reading: Figure 10 keeps higher-level contributions relatively stable while low-level employee contribution declines, matching the stated promotion tradeoff.
visualization_observations.next_action: Compare delayed, capacity-constrained, and external-hiring policies.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Check whether service-time spread changes task-5 outputs.
visualization_observations.exact_reading: Table 3 reports promoted count, average productivity, senior-manager productivity, and middle-manager number for l, 2l, and 3l service-time spread settings.
visualization_observations.next_action: Run replicated sweeps with uncertainty and raw values.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Audit the second sensitivity claim.
visualization_observations.exact_reading: Table 4 repeats every Table 3 value and still labels columns l, 2l, and 3l although the prose claims lower, median, and upper means.
visualization_observations.next_action: Treat the table as unresolved until independently regenerated.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Make omitted relationship information visible.
visualization_observations.exact_reading: Figure 11 places Human Capital and hometown networks on the same nodes and highlights a tie present in one layer but not the other.
visualization_observations.next_action: Collect observed layer edges and validate cross-layer predictions.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Turn extensions into inspectable operations.
visualization_observations.exact_reading: Jaccard measures simultaneous edges; evaluation and job vectors lead through Euclidean distance to an argmin position choice.
visualization_observations.next_action: Specify dimensions, scaling, missingness, outcomes, privacy, and fairness.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Keep contribution claims auditable.
visualization_observations.exact_reading: The paper links strengths to network complexity, sensitivity, and common sense, but offers no independent outcome validation.
visualization_observations.next_action: Downgrade correctness claims to bounded internal evidence.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: End the paper at its actual evidence boundary.
visualization_observations.exact_reading: The final two weaknesses admit incomplete personnel composition and common-sense parameters caused by few data, with sensitivity invoked only for slight changes.
visualization_observations.next_action: Carry both limitations into every reuse.
